title: Man. Post. Cap. VI: GAR many last ends if corruption turns all faculties
pass_a_gloss: GAR sets the moral-faculty fight aside and asks: if Adam's corruption turned the generative faculty to generation as a last end, and that corruption is universal, why not say it also turned the concoctive to concoction and the nutritive to nutrition as last ends—yielding as many last ends as faculties? Who who knows man's last end can be only one would bear that? The quarrel then is not whether generation is somehow moral, but whether Placeus multiplies last ends by the number of corrupted powers.
pass_b_english: GAR. But these things set aside, what is this—that Adam's corruption turned the generative faculty to generation as to a last end? For that corruption, being universal, infected the other faculties no less than this one. Why then should it not be said to have turned the other faculties to their acts—the concoctive to concoction, the nutritive to nutrition, &c.—as to a last end? so that for the number of faculties there would also be a number of last ends. Which of those who know that man's last end can be only one would bear that?
source_text: GAR. Verum his missis, quid est, quod dicitur Adae corruptio convertisse facultatem generatricem ad generationem tanquam finem ultimum? Nam illa certe corruptio, cum sit universalis, alias etiam facultates infecit non minus quam istam. Quidni ergo caeteras facultates ad actus suos, concoctricem ad concoctionem, altricem ad nutritionem, &c. tanquam finem ultimum convertisse dicatur? ut sit pro facultatum numero etiam finium ultimorum numerus. Quod quis ferat eorum qui norunt finem ultimum homini non posse esse nisi unum?

choices.choice: GAR: universal corruption would make many last ends
